blocks.text: Why video editors use Google Docs on Mac

Most video editors find that the actual cutting of footage takes less time than the setup. You spend your day managing client feedback, writing scripts, and tracking assets. Google Docs on Mac provides a stable environment for these tasks. It is free from the resource intensity of your video editing suite. You can keep a document open in Safari or Chrome alongside your timeline. This separation keeps your creative focus on the edit while your administrative tasks stay organized in the cloud.
Essential Google Docs shortcuts for Mac editors

Speed matters when you are bouncing between a timeline and a script. Using keyboard shortcuts saves you from reaching for the mouse. On your Mac, the Command key replaces the Control key found on other systems. Here are the ones you will use most often.
The Option + / command is particularly useful. If you forget where a specific formatting tool is, just type the name. It saves you from digging through the top menu bar.
Managing project feedback in Google Docs

Revision cycles are the leading cause of delays in video production. Instead of hunting through long email threads, create a feedback document for each project. Use a table to track the timestamp, the requested change, and the status. You can link this document in your project management app. When a client sends notes, paste them directly into the table. This gives you a clear checklist to work through while you edit.
How to handle file management bottlenecks

Nearly half of all editors struggle with file management. A Google Doc can act as your project manifest. Use it to list where your raw footage, audio assets, and project files live across your external drives. If you use tools like Hazel to automate your file sorting, keep a reference sheet in your Doc. This ensures you always know where your assets are stored without guessing.

Writing scripts in Google Docs allows for easy collaboration. You can share the link with your client or director to get instant feedback. Use the Suggestion mode to track changes without altering the original text. This keeps the creative process transparent and organized.
Using Lazur to work faster in Google Docs

Lazur sits in your Mac notch and helps you manage your workflow without breaking your rhythm. When you are deep in a script and need to find a specific menu option, hold the shortcut and ask. Lazur will point at the tool for you. If you need to draft a quick email to a client about a project update, use the dictation feature. It formats your speech into clean text directly in your browser.

items: Not using offline mode: You might lose work if your connection drops. Turn on offline mode in your browser settings.

faq.question: Is there an official Google Docs app for Mac?
faq.answer: No. Google Docs is a web-based service. You access it through a web browser like Chrome or Safari.

faq.question: How do I work on Google Docs without internet?
faq.answer: You need to use Google Chrome, install the Google Docs Offline extension, and enable offline access in your Google Drive settings.

faq.question: Can I use voice dictation in Google Docs on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. You can use the built-in macOS dictation or hold the fn key to use Lazur to dictate text directly into your document.

faq.question: How large can my Google Doc be?
faq.answer: A single document is limited to 1.02 million characters. This is plenty for most scripts and project notes.
